title: S&P Global Investment Manager Index (Dec 2026) — the publisher's own calendar now lists it Dec 8, a week before the derived Dec 15 date, ahead of the FOMC
source: EST: DERIVED BY RULE — the Tuesday eight days after the month's first Monday — which this session took from 9-for-9 to 12 FOR 12 across 34 months (Dec 2023 – Sep 2026) by recovering THREE primary mastheads no lane had ever read, all fetched direct 2026-09-09 with a browser UA: NOVEMBER 2025 (`81c1e32c73a143f5944dba8f641c7f48`, HTTP 200, 304,989 bytes, 'Embargoed until 1000 EST (1500 UTC) 11 November 2025', collected 'November 3-6, 2025') — the only prior fall-back-crossing edition, which sp-global-investment-manager-index-2026-11-10 logged as PERMANENTLY UNREACHABLE and named as the one-fetch upgrade to its leg 2; DECEMBER 2025 (`a8c4d63fbcba43e7b5ad13e7b2aff80a`, HTTP 200, 229,058 bytes, 'Embargoed until 1000 EST (1500 UTC) 9 December 2025', collected 'December 1-4, 2025') — this event's own calendar-month analogue, and the second consecutive EST edition after a fall-back, exactly the position December 2026 occupies; and JULY 2024 (`86ce2896f22c44bcb6fffff3010f4acf`, HTTP 200, 364,410 bytes, collected '1-4 July 2024'), whose date fits the rule and whose TIME DOES NOT — it reads 'Embargoed until 0001 EDT (0401 UTC) 9 July 2024'. December 2026's first Monday is 2026-12-07, giving 2026-12-15 (a Tuesday; all 72 rule outputs 2021-2026 are Tuesdays, checked mechanically). TIME: 15:00 UTC = 10:00 EST is quoted verbatim from three EST-month mastheads now (2023-12-12, 2025-11-11, 2025-12-09) and from 2026-01-13 — but the base rate is 10 OF 11 READ MASTHEADS, not 11 of 11, because July 2024 released at 00:01 ET. S&P Global's PMI calendar (pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Release/ReleaseDates?language=en, fetched direct 2026-09-09, HTTP 200, 23,858 bytes) is a rolling [today+2, today+28] window running 'September 11' to 'October 07', so December is not readable and will not be until roughly 2026-11-17. Written as the canonical file by the never-assessed initial research of this event, 2026-09-09, from the single proposal that existed (`proposals/sp-global-investment-manager-index-2026-12-15.from-sp-global-investment-manager-index-2026-11-10.json`, now inert). Estimate for the one honest reason its three siblings give: no publisher statement of this date exists at all. UPDATE 2026-11-15 — THE DERIVED DATE IS SUPERSEDED BY THE PUBLISHER'S OWN FORWARD CALENDAR: pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Release/ReleaseDates?language=en, fetched direct twice 2026-11-15 with a browser UA (HTTP 200, 24,406 bytes; the window now runs 'November 22' to 'December 10'), lists '15:00 UTC S&P Global Investment Manager Index' under the 'December 08' heading, after '01:01 UTC AIB Ireland Construction PMI' and before 'December 09'. 2026-12-08 is a Tuesday, one day after the first Monday (12-07), so the eight-days-after-first-Monday rule (12 for 12 on masthead evidence) FAILS on its first live December use; the date field moves from 2026-12-15 to 2026-12-08 and the id keeps its slug (the file is named by id, as with cbrs-q3-2026-results-2026-11-11). Stays `estimate`, as the 11-10 sibling did on the same listing: it is a calendar row, no masthead exists before release, and the same page had mirrored a stale UTC annotation before (11-10 masthead read 1000 EST (1400 UTC)). Checked 2026-11-15.
notes: THE PROPOSAL'S OWN PREMISE IS REFUTED, AND THAT IS THIS EVENT'S FINDING. It was filed as 'the control month: same rule, CPI five days earlier, no collision.' There is no control. (1) THE DAY STILL COLLIDES WITH BLS — `ppi-2026-12-15` is `confirmed`, `BLS:`, 08:30 ET, and shares 2026-12-15. November's lane called the collision structural but named it CPI's; the band is BLS's PRICE-PRINT band, which holds both series. All EIGHT BLS price prints this calendar tracks — CPI 09-11, 10-14, 11-10, 12-10 and PPI 09-10, 10-15, 11-13, 12-15 — fall inside the rule's own 9th-15th output window, so the IMI collides with one of them in 2 of the 4 months tracked and lands within 1-4 days in the other 2. (2) SAME-DAY COUNT IS 6, IDENTICAL TO NOVEMBER'S: PPI (medium), `empire-state-mfg-2026-12-15` (08:30 ET), `tic-monthly-2026-12-15` (16:00 ET), `uk-labour-market-2026-12-15`, `pjm-capacity-auction-2026-12`. (3) THE CORRIDOR IS THE DENSEST OF THE LADDER — 40 tracked entries within +/-5 days (15 before / 6 same-day / 19 after) against November's 23, with five high-impact: CPI 12-10, the CR expiry and funding deadline 12-11, retail sales 12-16, and quarterly triple-witching `opex-2026-12-18`. THE COLLISION MOVED TO THE FIELD WINDOW, WHICH IS THE UPGRADE. Nine verified collection windows now (three recovered this session), 7 of 9 closing Thursday and 6 of 9 running exactly Mon-Thu of the first-Monday week; applied here that is Dec 7-10, base case closing Thursday 2026-12-10. That window CONTAINS `fomc-2026-12-09` (confirmed, high, SEP + dot plot, 14:00 ET) and CLOSES ON CPI MORNING (`cpi-2026-12-10`, confirmed, 08:30 ET) — and it sits wholly inside the FOMC communications blackout, which runs 2026-11-28 through 2026-12-10. NO IMI PANEL IN ELEVEN EDITIONS READ HAS EVER BEEN POLLED ACROSS AN FOMC DECISION; the nearest miss is December 2025, whose window closed five days before that meeting and which still jumped +18% to +34% on 'the expectation of lower interest rates'. This panel is the most rate-sensitive object in the read set (Oct 2025: -26% to +4% on one cut) and December 2026 is the first time it answers with the dots in hand. NOT A TRADE: `symbols` is empty, no macro-keyed house playbook, no published consensus for a sentiment survey, status is `estimate`. THE TAPE QUESTION STAYS CLOSED — the sibling's n=68 null reproduced independently here (SPY p=0.428 vs their 0.433, QQQ 0.795 vs 0.803), and the one new conditional test this session ran (does an IMI day inside an expiry week move more?) FAILED ITS OWN CONTROLS: SPY p=0.038 within-IMI, but IMI-expiry vs OTHER expiry-week days p=0.478 and expiry weeks vs non-expiry weeks p=0.760, with QQQ null throughout. Triple-witching week is a narrative confound here, not a measured one. NO SUCCESSOR IS PROPOSED. The November lane closed the chain at four editions deliberately; that holds, and this session found no new dated event outside the calendar to propose. If the December edition releases on any date other than 2026-12-15, or at any time other than 15:00 UTC, this entry is derived from a broken rule and should be corrected by whoever finds it. UPDATE 2026-11-15 (pulse): THE DATE MOVED TO 2026-12-08 ON THE PUBLISHER'S OWN LISTING, so most of the geometry above is superseded. (1) The PPI collision is gone: `ppi-2026-12-15` is a week later, so December is, for the first time, a release day with no BLS price print on it, and the 'control that fails' framing no longer describes the day. (2) The panel is now most likely polled BEFORE the FOMC: a Tuesday 12-08 release implies a Mon-Thu window of roughly Nov 30-Dec 3, ahead of jobs 12-04, the 12-08/09 meeting and CPI 12-10, so 'the first panel polled across an FOMC decision with dots' is expected to FAIL, not pass (estimate; the window is only stated on the masthead). (3) 12-08 is FOMC day 1, with `spcx-lockup-expiry-2026-12-08` (high, confirmed) and `productivity-costs-q3-revised-2026-12-08` on the same date. (4) The panel will answer into a December hike that CME priced near 88.7% (25bp) / 11.3% (50bp) after the hot 10-CPI print on 11-10 (search-grade, approximate), so the Risk Appetite reading is a read of a market already braced for the hike. Nothing here is a trade: `symbols` is empty, no consensus exists, the date is `estimate`.
